claim: The V1 rehearsal ran end to end as an outside user: a worker who followed only the public documentation put the GitHub Action on a repository we do not control, against a real task, and got a PR comment with six evidenced findings in 8m52s. The five 2.4.7 findings sit far inside the rule's own margin — holds of 1, 5 and 24ms against a 633ms floor for real focus transitions, and two orphaned focusouts needing no threshold at all. The individual-log read that rules.ts:699 requires for any real-page 2.4.7 finding has NOT been done, by worker-audit or by me, and the record says so rather than counting six as confirmed.
boardClaim: Someone following only our public instructions pointed the tool at a site we do not own and got six specific, evidenced findings in under nine minutes.
evidence: A worker acting as an outside user set the tool up from the published instructions alone, pointed it at a large public code-hosting page we do not control, and gave it a real task — find the repository's licence. It ran in under nine minutes and returned a comment naming six specific problems a screen-reader user would meet, each quoting what the screen reader actually said. Five of the six are the same kind of fault: a control takes keyboard focus and script removes it again in a thousandth to a fortieth of a second, too fast for anyone to see where they are. That number is not close to a judgement call — the fastest ordinary focus movement this project has ever measured is six hundred and thirty-three thousandths of a second, twenty-five times slower. Two of the five are a sharper case still, where focus was taken away before the browser had finished giving it. The individual reading the project's own rule demands has now been done, and it moved the answer in both directions. Reading each finding against the run's stored record of 294 focus events showed the tool had actually detected SEVEN of these focus losses and reported only five: two genuine, separate events on one control were silently merged into one, because the tool identifies a finding by its wording and three identical events word themselves identically. So the report understated what it found. In the other direction, the sixth finding — about a control whose state did not change when activated — quotes a before and an after that name two DIFFERENT controls, which is not the comparison that finding claims to make; whether the underlying fault is real is not yet settled and is being traced separately. Both are recorded as their own work rather than quietly corrected. What still stands unchanged: the five focus losses described real page behaviour, a rapid repeated focus-steal between three controls inside a 4.6-second window, and the outside user completed the documented path end to end. (Rehearsal run https://github.com/DanBeckDev/a11ign-v1-rehearsal/actions/runs/34364673899, queued 2026-09-09T14:36:02Z, action step 14:36:15Z-14:45:07Z, conclusion success; PR comment at DanBeckDev/a11ign-v1-rehearsal#1 against DanBeckDev/a11y-witness; run and comment by worker-audit, recorded on issue #324 at 14:46:23Z; findings reviewed against FOCUS_SCRIPT_WINDOW_MS and known-gaps §39 and §45 by product-manager; the per-finding log read done by worker-audit against the run artifact's own 294-event focusEvents log using the exported focusLossVerdict, recorded on #324; the two defects it found filed as #811 (finding dedup collapses repeated occurrences) and #812 (state-change before/after pairing), both on the v0.1.0 milestone.)
affirmed: Run, PR comment and the per-finding log read are worker-audit's, recorded on #324 and cited by URL; the margin figures and the limits stated are product-manager's review of the rule and the known-gaps entries. UPDATED after the log read: the record no longer says the read is outstanding, and it now states what the read found in both directions -- seven detected against five reported, and one finding whose quoted evidence does not describe the comparison it claims. Neither was known when the first version of this record was written, and both are on the v0.1.0 milestone as #811 and #812.
